hourly.summary: Arsenal fans are satisfied but not euphoric after a routine 2-0 win over Everton that sends them top of the table level on points with City. The defensive solidity (clean sheet, Gabriel and Konsa dominant) and Gyokeres' influence are praised, but the familiar frustration resurfaces: 20 shots, only 4 on target, and an attacking unit still deemed wasteful despite the three points. The Emirates roof leak added farcical chaos to an otherwise professional afternoon — capped off by the women's NLD win for a clean sweep.

daily.summary: Arsenal fan sentiment plummeted dramatically across the day, shifting from early-morning buzz (8/10) over tactical mastery against Bayern and a potential Bruno Guimarães coup, to hopeful but cautious optimism (7/10) after the Allianz draw, then crashing to edgy anxiety (4/10) as Saka's injury severity emerged and ESPN wrote off the title charge. By evening, the mood settled into deep anxiety (4/10) with the 6-8 week Saka absence confirmed, academy departures stinging, and transfer rumors feeling hollow.

weekly.summary: The week began in injury-induced crisis, spiked to euphoria after a statement Champions League win, then crashed violently when the club announced 60 redundancies amid record revenues and a massive Arteta contract — a betrayal narrative that reframed all subsequent on-pitch success. A brief optimistic rebound mid-week faded into conflicted, grudging acceptance as Arsenal topped the table with 'ugly' pragmatic wins, leaving fans torn between results and a gnawing sense that the club's soul has been corporatized. The dominant arc is extreme volatility anchored by a core fracture between sporting dominance and institutional trust.
